newsitem.title: INDIA: India's GAIL receives 15-16 bids for joint venture.
newsitem.headline: India's GAIL receives 15-16 bids for joint venture.

text.p: India's Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL) said on Wednesday it had recieved 15-16 bids to set up a joint venture for supply of liquified natural gas (LNG) as part of a $10 billion project to diversify India's energy needs.
"We have received 15 to 16 international bids," state-run GAIL's chairman C.R. Prasad told a news conference in the Indian capital.
India's GAIL, state-run firms Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) and Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) will together hold a 50 percent stake in the project, Prasad said.
The bids are currently being examined by officials of IOC, GAIL and ONGC, he added.
"Hopefully in the next few months something will firm up," Prasad said.
Prasad said the Oman-India subsea natural gas pipeline project has not been abandoned.
"On the Indo-Oman pipeline, GAIL is working," Prasad said.
He said a team of officials from GAIL and the Petroleum Ministry will visit Oman to access the work there "and see what further work can be done on the project".
